rules.text: never schedule **Sunday, Monday, or Saturday**. Monday is held open as an emergency reserve. Work is booked **Tuesday–Friday** only.
details: "Today" is never used either — except a job whose stated preferred date is today, or a past-due job that needs the soonest slot.

rules.text: roughly **8:00 AM – 5:30 PM Pacific**. Times are stored with the Pacific time-zone offset (e.g. `2026-06-25T09:00:00-07:00`).

**Fill the nearest open days first**, packing densely from 8 AM, then a daily **compaction pass** pulls later jobs into the earliest open slots. Keep about a **30-minute buffer** between jobs and never double-book a tech.
details: Busy time is read from the tech's **entire** calendar (including turns), so it never books on top of an all-day turn.
Compaction is idempotent — once everything is packed, a re-run changes nothing.

rules.text: Emergency / Urgent → High → Normal / Medium → Low.
if a job's scheduled time passes without completion, reschedule it to the next available slot (keeping priority order). Never leave a past-due job unscheduled.

Emergency and Urgent melds are sorted to the front of the queue and scheduled on today's date (the current day), overriding the Monday and "no today" restrictions. They land at the first available slot of the day (8am or first open slot). All other melds continue to respect the Tue–Fri rule and never land on today. Sat/Sun remain blocked even for emergencies.
**Preference lock — honor a stated day/time/date.** If a work order's **title or chat** asks for a specific day, time, or date, the scheduler books it there and won't move it.
details: Locked jobs are exempt from compaction, blocked-day moves, and overlap moves — a stated preference is never overridden by packing.
Ordinal dates are understood ("June 18th"). A stated date of **today** books same-day; a date in the **past** is dropped (job scheduled ASAP).
Only the **title** and a genuine **chat request** count — office-hours boilerplate ("Mon–Fri 9–5") is never treated as a preference.

rules.text: **Reads the chat.** It reads each job's recent messages for reschedule requests, resident preferred times, and duration hints, and accommodates residents when possible (without overriding Emergency/Urgent).
details: A Claude "chat reader" interprets the intent; the code still applies every rule above. If it's unavailable, a keyword reader is the fallback.

**Not-yet-scheduled** jobs honor requests from the last **30 days**; **already-scheduled** jobs only act on messages from the last **~26 hours** (so an old message doesn't re-shuffle the calendar every day).
"Earlier / sooner / before Monday" means **avoid** that day and find an earlier slot — not book on it.
Duration hints are only trusted between **15 minutes and 4 hours** (avoids reading "within 48 hours" as a 48-hour job).

rules.text: don't reshuffle without a reason — only move work for a higher priority, a past-due job, or a valid resident conflict.
any appointment that lands on a reserved day (Mon/Sat/Sun) or that double-books a tech is automatically relocated.
always dry-run a change first. Live runs happen only in the cloud (see "How it runs").
**Only Jonas Hoard and Armani Mitchell work Tacoma.** Jonas takes all non-turn repairs; Armani takes turns.
details: Any non-turn tc68/tc34 job found on a different tech is **reassigned to Jonas** (e.g. Margarito is Tri-Cities, not Tacoma).

rules.text: **Jonas does every work type here, including lawn / Environmental** — unlike Spokane, grounds work at tc68/tc34 is not split off to anyone else.
**Turns** (project melds) go to Armani; the repair scheduler leaves them alone. (Dulce Salinas legitimately appears on "AppFolio Estimate" turn melds.)
**All repairs go to Justin Gutierrez.** Wade Hippen no longer works here — any job still sitting on Wade is reclaimed and reassigned to Justin.

**Justin's day ends at 4:00 PM**, not the general 5:00 PM cutoff — no job is scheduled to end after 16:00 (requested by Justin, 2026-07-01). A hard-pinned title/chat date that doesn't fit with the normal buffer gets squeezed in with a tighter (or zero) buffer that day instead of running the day later — the close time never moves, even for a non-negotiable date.
**Covers** the Spokane property group plus Our Natural Homes.
turns, Environmental (those go to the grounds team), and pest. Unassigned pest is never auto-assigned.
**Only reclaim** a repair from the turn techs (Scott Higley, Ron Cramer, Micheal Magoon) when they're wrongly holding a plain repair, or from unassigned non-pest jobs.
details: **Leave alone:** David & Alexander (grounds), **Florencia** (pest), and Dulce (estimates) — those assignments are intentional.

rules.text: when a job needs the tenant present, the scheduler reads the tenant's chosen availability windows and books inside one.
**Pest "attend treatment" jobs** are date-pinned: the date is fixed and the exact time is vendor-driven (left to a person).
Only **one appointment per job** is kept — duplicate appointments are cleaned up so they can't cause double-booking.

rules.category: Emergency/Urgent always goes FIRST on today's calendar (rewritten 2026-07-02)
rules.text: an emergency is never wedged into whatever gap happens to be free — it takes the earliest available time today, and whatever else is already on today's calendar shifts LATER that same day to make room (`insertEmergencyToday`). An already-committed today appointment is **never** moved to a different date for this — the resident is expecting Justin today regardless, so the day's close time can stretch past the normal 4pm, up to **6pm** (`EMERGENCY_EXTENDED_CLOSE`), instead. A today job with a stated resident preference/lock is left in place, never shifted.

the 30-minute buffer between jobs exists for drive time between properties — back-to-back jobs at the SAME property (e.g. two units in the same building) need no buffer, since Justin is already on site. The buffer only applies between jobs at different properties. This applies everywhere a slot is searched, including the emergency shift above and the same-day gap-closing pass below.

plain new/past-due repairs (no chat/pref/emergency trigger) are placed by building CODE PREFIX (e.g. "k104"), not pure priority+earliest-slot — the goal is Justin spending a whole day at one property instead of bouncing around. A new job first looks for an existing future day already dedicated to its property with room; if none, it starts a fresh day on the nearest completely open work day; if neither is possible within 90 days, it falls back to the plain earliest-slot search so nothing goes unscheduled.
details: **Never moves the DATE of an already-scheduled job.** The only exception is same-day gap-closing (`sameDayCompaction`): every day is swept for gaps that no longer need to exist — a cancellation leaving a hole mid-day, or (since 2026-07-02) a same-property pair still carrying a buffer from before the property-aware rule existed — and the jobs after the gap (same day only, not preference-locked) shift earlier to close it. This is what replaced the old cross-day compaction, which used to undo clustering by pulling melds to the nearest open slot regardless of property.
Chat-driven reschedules and preference locks are unaffected by clustering — they keep their existing (higher-priority) behavior and can break a day's property theme for that one visit.
One-time backlog rebuild done 2026-07-01 via `pm_spokane_property_test.js` (kept in the repo as the reference implementation / for any future one-time re-clustering; not run automatically).

**Cross-day gap-filling (`pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js`, added 2026-07-02) — MANUAL only, not in any workflow.** A day that isn't fully booked 8am-4pm delays the backlog and eats an extra calendar day for no reason. Run this by hand (`DRY_RUN=1 node pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js` to preview, `node pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js` live) to pull melds forward from later days into a day's open tail time, in this order: (a) more of that day's own property from the nearest later day, (b) a complete different-property day/group that fits the gap entirely, (c) loose singles (priority, then oldest-created first) — capped to one per source day (its current last job) so a pull never leaves a fresh gap behind. Skips today, locked/preference melds, and Emergency/Urgent. Kept manual deliberately (per Florencia, 2026-07-02) until it's been watched working correctly for a while — it moves already-scheduled jobs across dates, which is exactly what the "never move an already-scheduled date" rule above normally forbids.

rules.text: **David Sanchez and Alexander Overall** handle recurring "Lawn service" melds in Spokane (plus Our Natural Homes). Repairs and other techs' work are not touched.
Each week's recurring lawn melds are snapped to a **canonical template week** (a fixed day, time, and duration per property) and mirrored forward **+7 days**, so the times never drift week to week.
details: A property lands on the calendar as often as PropertyMeld generates its instance — most are weekly; a few (e.g. h731) are intentionally bi-weekly.
A new recurrence not yet in the template is flagged as UNKNOWN so it can be added to the template.
